schema.title: Findings
schema.description: What a source, such as a vulnerability matcher, found in a manifest.

version.description: The version of the source's database.

matches.description: One entry for each vulnerability in each package. Empty when the source found nothing.

id.description: <vulnerabilityID>/<packageID>. Left out where it would be too long.

vulnerabilityID.description: The CVE where one exists, and else the ID of the advisory.

packageID.description: The ID of the package in the SBOM that the match was made from.

packageVersion.description: Left out for a package that has none.

severity.description: The source's own: such as Critical, High, Medium, Low, Negligible or Unknown.

fixState.description: The source's own: such as fixed, not-fixed, wont-fix or unknown. Empty when the source says nothing.

fixTarget.description: The lowest fixed version above the installed one, in the package's own version scheme. Left out where none is known.

updateTarget.description: The highest fixTarget of the package's matches in the manifest.

aliases.description: The IDs of the related vulnerabilities, sorted, never the match's own ID.

knownExploited.description: True when the source lists the vulnerability as known to be exploited.

epssPermille.description: The EPSS score in per mille: floor(score x 1000). Left out where the source has none.

epssDate.description: The date of the EPSS score, as the source writes it.

version.description: The version of CVSS, such as 3.1.

schema.title: Description
schema.description: What a vulnerability database holds for one vulnerability, from each of its providers, and whether each package that it was asked about has the fix of a provider. The strings are the database's own.

vulnerabilityID.description: The ID that the database was asked about.

aliases.description: The IDs of the same vulnerability that the records name, such as the CVE of a GitHub advisory, sorted.

cvss.description: The vectors of the records' scores, each once.

knownExploited.description: True when a record lists the vulnerability as known to be exploited.

epssPermille.description: The EPSS score of the vulnerability's CVE in per mille: floor(score x 1000). Left out where the database has none.

epssDate.description: The date of the EPSS score.

references.description: The URLs that the records name, each once.

packages.description: The packages that the database was asked about, as they were given.

providers.description: What each provider says of a fix: the entries that answer for an asked package, and for a package that none answers for, some that name it. Empty when there are none.

otherProviders.description: The entries that the list of providers leaves out, counted per provider, sorted by provider. Each says Unknown for every asked package.

version.description: The version of CVSS, such as 3.1.

type.description: Syft's type of the package, such as deb, rpm, apk or go-module.

purl.description: The purl, which names the source package in the qualifier upstream and the release in distro.

distro.description: The distribution and its release, such as debian-12, where the purl names none, and the purl's where it does.

vulnerabilityID.description: The ID of the vulnerability whose records the answer rests on: the ID asked about, or one that its records name.

namespace.description: Grype's namespace, such as debian:distro:debian:12 or github:language:go.

package.description: The name of the package that the provider lists, or the CPE that NVD lists.

fixState.description: Grype's: fixed when the provider names a fix, else not-fixed, wont-fix or not-affected. Empty when the provider says nothing.

packages.description: The answer for each asked package.

fixedForInstalled.description: Yes: the provider speaks for the package's distribution or ecosystem, no range that it lists holds the installed version, and the installed version is at a fixed version or above. No: such a provider lists a range that holds it. Unknown: anything else.

operations.name: match
operations.description: Matches the packages of a manifest's SBOM against the vulnerability database: the findings of the manifest, with severities, fixes, known exploitation and CVSS vectors.

parameterSchema.description: match takes no parameters: the SBOM of the manifest, which it is given as its input, is all it needs.

operations.name: describe
operations.description: Describes a vulnerability from the vulnerability database, offline: the description, CVSS, known exploitation, EPSS and references, and what each provider says of a fix, per distribution release or ecosystem. For each package given, fixedForInstalled says whether the provider of the package's own distribution or ecosystem has fixed it at the installed version: Yes, No or Unknown. Only the entries that answer for a package given are listed, and the entries that name a package that none answers for, at most 8 for each; the entries that answer for no package given are counted per provider in otherProviders. The advisory of a language package is often listed under the ecosystem's own ID, such as a GHSA or GO ID, which the case file may name: give it and the other IDs of the vulnerability in aliases.

parameterSchema.description: The vulnerability to describe, and the packages of the case to compare with each provider's fix.

vulnerabilityID.description: A vulnerability ID or an alias, such as CVE-2026-0001 or GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.

aliases.description: Other IDs of the same vulnerability, such as the IDs that the case's findings carry. They are searched with vulnerabilityID.

packages.description: The packages of the case, as the SBOM has them. Give the purl: it names the source package that distributions track, and the release.

type.description: Syft's type, such as deb, rpm, apk or go-module.

distro.description: The distribution and release, such as debian-12, where the purl names none. Where it names one, the same.

settingsSchema.description: How the vulnerabilities collector keeps its vulnerability database and how many SBOMs it matches at once. A setting that is left out takes its default.

maxConcurrent.description: How many SBOMs are matched at once: a match that finds them all busy waits for one. 2 by default, which is as many matches as the hub's assessor asks for at once.

databaseUpdates.description: Online updates the database, through the proxy of the collector's environment, when it has none and whenever the schedule database fires (spec.triggers). Offline never updates it: the database is the one that is there, or the seed. Online by default.

seedDatabase.description: The absolute path of a directory that holds a database, such as the one that the image carries for a cluster without internet. When the database directory holds no database, it is copied there before the database is loaded, once the collector has its settings.
